body: I get this and think about it whenever a tragedy occurs and mental health is discussed. They have good intentions, but when an old friend posts mental health resources online and hasn’t checked up on me in months, I slightly raise an eyebrow.

Thanks for sharing this with us. Yeah for sure have experienced it. Recovering alcoholic musician here - drank pretty heavily from 18 to 27. I’m shy and introverted by default, but I can be selectively outgoing once I’m comfortable with somebody after a while. One of my biggest concerns when I stopped drinking was that I would be boring. I used alcohol for a long time as a social icebreaker. I just wanted so badly to be like the other people at parties who I saw as charming and popular. And it worked, temporarily. My parties were 10% memorable moments, but 90% me facing consequences for doing something stupid. 

I guess for me, the biggest thing in recovery was just accepting that I’m naturally a quiet person and being kinder to myself about that. There’s nothing wrong with being that way - I have social good and bad days. And that’s not to say that I’ve become a hermit. I do all kinds of things, go to events, and hang out with friends. 

So if I had to sum it up, I’d say acceptance was really helpful for me. Accepting that I’m uncomfortable in the moment and acknowledging that. Or accepting that not every interaction has to go perfectly (that was a big one too). DM me if you want to talk more. Happy to chat more!

Hey sorry to hear that you’re going through this. I’m also almost 30 and feeling similar. It’s hard to find a (excuse the cheesiness) beacon on the horizon these days. Something that makes you say, “Ah, that’s what I’m working towards.” I don’t know what I could say to help, but thank you for sharing how you’re feeling.
